text:
elaine: heads up - I'm kicking off an experiment to smooth queue draining across clusters to reduce p99 spikes from cross-zone spillovers. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/queue-smooth patch: https://phab.redwood/D123

elaine: motivation: when a zone is saturated we spill to another region; buckets get drained aggressively causing KV cache cold misses and kernel re-select thrashing -> p99 latency spikes.

todd: +1. can you paste the smoothing config? curious about token budget math.

elaine: config I'm testing:
```yaml
queue_policy:
  strategy: priority-smoothing
  smoothing_window_ms: 300
  cross_zone_spill_fraction: 0.15
  token_budget_target_per_core: 1200
  drain_rate_alpha: 0.6
``` 

shyam: nice. what's the expected batch formation change? will batching wait longer? risk higher p50?

elaine: we cap wait to 120ms for small requests, but allow adaptive join for midsize. expected p50 ~ same, p95 down, p99 down. tradeoff: slight throughput hit when fully loaded.

infra-bot: perf-run started (id: run-2026-03-14-09). collecting kernel-selection logs and kv cache stats.

katie: can we get kernel selection trace? last week we saw a kernel flip flop between int8-v1 and int8-v2 on sequence length 256 causing 20% token/sec variance.

elaine: yes. run includes `--trace-kernel-decisions` and `--kv-profiling=heatmap`. sample snippet from trace:
```
[trace] seq_len=256 selected_kernel=int8-v2 reasons: memory_bandwidth_est 0.78, conv_cost 0.45
[trace] seq_len=300 selected_kernel=int8-v1 reasons: reduced_gemm_tiling
[warning] kernel_switches=9 in 60s
```

dave: KV hits look promising on first pass? what's hit rate when smoothing is on vs baseline?

infra-bot: kv-stats(before): hit_rate=64.2%, avg_lookup_ms=1.9
infra-bot: kv-stats(after-60s): hit_rate=77.8%, avg_lookup_ms=1.5

todd: wow that's a good jump. Which component caused fewer cold fills? batching or reduced spill bursts?

elaine: mostly batching + calmer drain reduces eviction churn. we also reduced per-shard token_budget to avoid aggressive eviction. config diff:
```diff
- token_budget_target_per_core: 2000
+ token_budget_target_per_core: 1200
```

katie: p99 numbers?

infra-bot: baseline p99=1120ms, experiment p99=640ms (60s window); p95 baseline=220ms -> 210ms

shyam: verifying kernel overhead: we added a 3ms scheduling step in scheduler to compute smoothing weights. does that matter?

elaine: measured scheduling overhead added ~2.8ms on avg, but it's parallel to batch formation so not on critical path for most requests. net win.

dave: any regression signals for embedders or rerank pipelines?

elaine: rerank latency unchanged. embedder p50 +5ms but p99 unchanged. cost per token increased 1.2% due to smaller batch utilization on green periods.

todd: next steps? roll to canary in prod region us-west-2 with canary=5% for 1h and watch p99/kv-hit/kernel_switches.

elaine: yup. I'll post canary link when live. tagging @shyam for kernel watch and @katie for eval sets.

katie: ack. will run eval set 18 against both baselines and experiment for hallucination / quality checks.

elaine: action items: (1) canary 5% us-west-2 1h (me) (2) kernel trace monitor (shyam) (3) evals (katie) (4) cost delta estimate (dave)

dave: assigning cost delta, will post numbers in ~30m.

infra-bot: canary started (id: canary-1815000000-1) :rocket:

elaine: thanks team :thumbsup: will update after 1h.
